subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ramp — tranche mapping and velocity request
messages:
From: Asha Reddy <asha@peregrine.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Greene <tgreene@peregrine.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Multi-year Dedicated ramp — initial requirements

Karthik,

Thanks for the conversation earlier. Per our internal planning, we expect to scale inference usage from a pilot (4 A100-equivalent GPUs / ~60 TPM) to production (40 A100-equivalent GPUs / ~600 TPM) over 18 months. Our procurement team is evaluating a 3-year committed prepay with an annual true-up.

Key asks: 
- Prefer a phased onramp that frontloads some capacity in Q1-2 of Year 1 to support commercial launch.
- Looking for a blended term discount vs month-to-month — target overall discount in the 22–28% range depending on commit pattern.
- Need clarity on how token/TMP overages are handled and when we can swap model variants (quantized vs fp16) without penalty.

I attached our requirement sheet. Can you share a sample tranche schedule and indicative pricing for 3yr vs 1yr? Also flag any gating items (SLA, data residency, SOC 2 scoping) that might affect timeline.

Best,
Asha
Asha Reddy
Head of Platform — Peregrine AI

[attachment: Peregrine_MultiYear_Requirements.xlsx]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Reddy <asha@peregrine.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Multi-year Dedicated ramp — tranche mapping and velocity request

Asha — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. Quick read-through below and attaching a draft tranche-based schedule + indicative pricing (high level).

Top-level options we recommend:
1) 3-year phased prepay (recommended for cost predictability) — staggered tranches with a frontloaded Year 1 tranche to cover commercial launch (40% of committed capacity available in first 6 months), then two equal tranches in Y1-Y2 to reach target capacity. Blended discount target: 24% modeled.
2) 1-year prepay with optional annual top-up — higher unit price, preserves flexibility; modeled discount ~12% depending on TPM bands.

Variant notes: swapping to a quantized variant is allowed after an initial 90-day stabilization window for each major model version; overages billed at the committed unit rate + 20% uplift unless you enable burst pools (we can map that into the SOW).

I attached the PDF with tranche mapping, milestone acceptance criteria, and an initial commercial table. If you want more frontload we can rework to a 60% Q1-Q2 release, but that will push the blended discount slightly toward the lower end.

Next steps: if you can indicate preferred frontload %, I’ll run this by finance and legal for a commercial counter and formal SOW.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Exec — Redwood Inference

[attachment: RI-dedicated-tranche-pricing-v2.pdf]

From: Asha Reddy <asha@peregrine.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Greene <tgreene@peregrine.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T08:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Multi-year Dedicated ramp — tranche mapping and velocity request

Karthik — appreciate the options. Two clarifications from our side: 
1) We need 50% of the committed capacity online by the start of Q2 (we define that as 2027-04-01) to support customer SLAs. Is the 40% frontload still feasible?
2) The 24% blended discount is good — but we’ll need price protection / true-up mechanics if we commit to 3 years. Our procurement prefers an annual reconciliation (roll-forward) not a retrospective true-up.

If you can do 50% frontload in Q1–Q2 and include a roll-forward true-up (apply unused committed capacity as credit to subsequent year’s consumption rather than chargebacks), we can move the deal forward quickly.

Also, any chance for a one-time onboarding credit for model tuning / integration?

—Asha

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-03T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Peregrine ask — 50% frontload + roll-forward true-up request

Team — looping you in. Peregrine wants 50% of committed capacity available by 2027-04-01 (they started pilot in Jan). They’re asking for roll-forward true-ups (unused capacity turns into credit for the next year) and a one-time onboarding credit. 

Finance constraints: our standard model assumes 40% frontload for Year 1 for 3yr prepay. Moving to 50% bumps near-term cash impact and reduces realized margin in Year 1. We can trade a tighter SLA window or milestone-linked payments (e.g., 25% up-front, 25% on Q2 milestone) to protect cash.

Legal: need to confirm the roll-forward mechanism language (we usually do retrospective true-ups). I think we can do roll-forward if we cap carry-forward credits to 25% of next-year consumption and require that credits are consumed within 12 months.

Marissa — can you model the blended discount at 50% frontload for 3yr at 22% blended (vs the 24% baseline) and include a one-time $75k onboarding credit? How much does that change margin and does that stay within approval thresholds?

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-04T14:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Peregrine ask — 50% frontload + roll-forward true-up request

Karthik / team — ran the numbers. Summary:
- 50% frontload (vs 40%) for 3yr commit reduces NPV by ~4.2 percentage points at our cost curve assumptions. Blended discount required to hit their target bandwidth drops from 24% to ~22% if we keep onboarding credit at $75k.
- If we limit roll-forward carry to 25% of next-year committed consumption (expire after 12 months) and require milestone acceptance to unlock each tranche, this mitigates revenue leakage materially.
- If Sales wants to increase discount to 25% (to sweeten the deal) we need director approval; otherwise 22% with 25% carry cap + $75k onboarding credit is approvable by commercial ops.

I’ll attach the P&L sensitivity in the HubSpot link and draft the clause for "carry-forward credit" to hand to Legal.

-Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Reddy <asha@peregrine.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-08T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Multi-year Dedicated ramp — tranche mapping and velocity request

Asha — thanks for the patience; quick update and proposed path forward.

1) Frontload: We can accommodate 50% of the committed capacity by 2027-04-01 under a tranche schedule that ties release to three milestone gates: (a) pilot acceptance (performance and latency SLOs), (b) security sign-off (SOC 2 scoping confirmation), and (c) network readiness (VPC peering completed). Those milestones will be spelled out in the SOW.

2) Economics: Commercial Ops modeled a blended discount of 22% with a $75k one-time onboarding credit. If Peregrine needs a 25% blended discount, we’ll need a director-level approval and a slightly larger annual commit or a longer escrowed payment profile.

3) True-up: We can implement a roll-forward carry-forward credit capped at 25% of next year’s committed capacity, expiring after 12 months. Any true-up beyond that will be billed as overage at committed unit rate + 20%.

4) Next steps: I’ll prepare a formal commercial counter and SOW with milestone definitions and the carry-forward language. If you’re comfortable with the 22% blended + $75k onboarding credit + 50% frontload gated by the three milestones, I’ll circulate for legal and draft a signature-ready DocuSign.

If you’d like me to scope the alternative (25% blended with director approval), I can run that as a parallel option but it will add ~2 business days to the internal approval loop.

Thanks — can you confirm which path you prefer?

Best,
Karthik
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
